notes: Free-text lines Medicus's edit-problem 'additionalInformation' field carries verbatim from GP2GP import that add no clinical meaning of their own -- pure boilerplate restating fields already captured structurally elsewhere on the problem (e.g. problemStatus/significance). additionalInformation is often multi-line (confirmed live 2026-07-25, real example: "ear\nActive Problem, Significant" -- 'ear' is a genuine free-text note, the second line is pure noise), so matching is done PER LINE (trimmed, case-insensitive exact match against this list), never against the whole field -- a genuine free-text line must never be silently dropped because the field ALSO happens to contain a generic one. Used by content-scripts/problem-description-cleanup.js's stripGenericAdditionalInfoLines() to offer removing just the matched line(s), keeping the rest of the field untouched. Add a new entry here to expand coverage -- no code change needed.

entries.rationale: GP2GP import boilerplate restating metadata already captured structurally on the problem itself (problemStatus:"Active", significance:"Major"/"Minor") -- confirmed on a real patient's problem list, carries no information not already available elsewhere on the record.

GP2GP import boilerplate: the source record carried no significance value, so the importer defaulted it to Minor and recorded that decision as a free-text line -- restates significance:"minor" already captured structurally on the problem, no clinical meaning. Confirmed real example ("Infantile eczema", 90823000, Read-v2 origin): additionalInformation "Unspecified Significance: Defaulted to Minor\nProblem severity: Minor". A "...Defaulted to Major" sibling is plausible by the same template but NOT yet seen on a real patient -- add it only once actually observed, don't guess it in.

Sibling boilerplate line to "Unspecified Significance: Defaulted to Minor" above, same real example, same restates-existing-metadata reasoning. A "Problem severity: Major" sibling is plausible but NOT yet seen on a real patient -- add it only once actually observed.
